message_id.description: Sender-assigned stable identity of one logical to-device message. Queue services MUST preserve it byte-for-byte across retries and redelivery. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id).

sender_principal_id.description: Sender Principal DID. Intentionally NOT named sender_actor_id: device messages are out-of-band per-device transport envelopes that travel principal-to-principal outside any Realm context, so the Realm-scoped Actor identity used by message.schema.json / event-payload.schema.json does not apply here. For a device sender, pair it with sender_device_id and verify that pair against the accepted PCR device projection; for a Native Agent sender it equals sender_agent_id and the signer is anchored by sender_agent_verification_method plus sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id.

sender_device_id.description: Authoring human device. Exactly one sender endpoint branch is present: this field, or the complete sender_agent_* triple. A Native Agent runtime has no device identity and MUST NOT be disguised as an ak:device (identity/contact-and-direct-conversation.md section 8.2.1, crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1), which is why the two are a closed XOR rather than one nullable device slot. Receivers deduplicate by (sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, message_id) for a device sender and by (sender_principal_id, sender_agent_id, message_id) for a Native Agent sender.

sender_agent_id.description: Native Agent principal that authored this message. Present exactly when the sender is an Agent runtime, together with sender_agent_verification_method and sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id. It equals sender_principal_id; carrying it explicitly is what makes the endpoint branch decidable from the envelope alone, matching the requester XOR of member_repair_request_content and the consume / claim_envelope XORs of crypto-media/device-lifecycle.md section 9.0.1.

sender_agent_verification_method.description: Verification method the Agent currently signs with. The device branch gets the equivalent from the accepted device projection; without this the receiver would hold an Agent principal id and no way to say which key speaks for it.

sender_agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Accepted Agent key authorization Event that anchors sender_agent_verification_method.

recipient_principal_id.description: Recipient Principal DID. Same naming rationale as sender_principal_id — device messages are not Realm-scoped, so Actor identity is not used. Pair with recipient_device_id for targeted device delivery.

device_proof.description: Optional per-device transport proof block (typical sub-fields: device_authorize_event_id, sender_device_key_fingerprint, signature_over_content_digest). It MUST NOT replace MLS authentication of the enclosing envelope and MUST NOT be trusted in isolation.

unsigned.description: Optional non-authenticated metadata block (transport-layer hints only). Receivers MUST NOT trust any field here for authorization, ordering, or cryptographic verification. Typical sub-fields: progress (delivery progress hint), error_context (transport-layer error diagnostics), retry_after_ms. By convention this block is excluded from the signed transcript of the enclosing transport envelope and is dropped on persist.

allOf.$comment: Closed sender endpoint XOR: either sender_device_id alone, or the complete sender_agent_* triple alone. A half-filled Agent branch, or a device id sitting next to an Agent id, would let a producer smuggle a second unauthenticated sender identity past the rule that an Agent is never spelled as an ak:device.

actor_private_update_kind.description: Closed DeviceMessageEnvelope.kind set for actor-private sibling-device projection updates. These values are transport discriminators, not Event kinds and never enter shared Realm history.

secret_request_content.description: ak.secret.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). A newly authorized device asks an existing authorized device to hand over an account-scope secret over HPKE. Carries no secret material itself.

request_id.description: Caller-generated random correlation id; MUST NOT be reused after the request is answered or cancelled.

secret_id.description: Opaque identifier of the requested secret, e.g. example_mls_account_secret.

from_device.description: Requesting (new) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: base64url X25519 HPKE public key the requesting device controls and the responder seals to. It MUST be byte-identical to the hpke_key registered for from_device in the current accepted device projection. A responder MUST fail closed on any mismatch and MUST NOT accept an ephemeral key merely because it appeared in a bound SAS verification transcript; SAS authenticates device signing keys, not HPKE sealing keys.

secret_send_content.description: ak.secret.send to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §10.7). The existing authorized device returns the requested secret HPKE-sealed to the requester's recipient_hpke_public_key. The plaintext is never visible to the queue service.

request_id.description: Correlates to the pending ak.secret.request; MUST equal the request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD. Receivers MUST drop sends that do not match a locally pending request_id.

secret_id.description: Opaque requested secret identifier; MUST equal the secret_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and HPKE AAD.

from_device.description: Authorizing (existing) device; MUST equal envelope sender_device_id and MUST be a non-revoked device of the recipient principal.

ciphertext.description: base64url HPKE AEAD ciphertext over the secret plaintext. The plaintext MUST carry the requested secret body, version, request_id and secret_id. The HPKE AAD is the RFC 8785 JCS canonical JSON of {message_id, kind, sender_principal_id, sender_device_id, recipient_principal_id, recipient_device_id, request_id, secret_id, expires_at}; expires_at is the exact already-validated canonical Arkret UTC millisecond string from DeviceMessageEnvelope and MUST NOT be converted to a second epoch field. Freshness for server-assigned sent_at is bound by the sender-assigned message_id plus the one-time request_id authenticated inside the sealed plaintext and AAD.

realm_key_request_content.description: ak.realm_key.request to-device content (device-lifecycle.md §13.2). A read-eligible receiver asks a concrete key source to evaluate policy and, if authorized, deliver historical history_secret material via durable ak.realm_key.share or an equivalent policy-authorized recovery path. Carries no key material itself.

recipient_hpke_public_key.description: Recipient device HPKE public key (KeyPackage init key or equivalent) the key source MUST verify as an authorized device key for recipient_principal_id before sealing history_secret.

requested_source_kind.description: Source class this request targets. key_backup is intentionally excluded because it is retrieved via ak.self.keys.backups.command.unlock.

target_source_ref.description: Concrete source this request is routed to: a device_id for own_device / verified_member_device, or a service DID for archive_node / recovery_service. Service-targeted reuse of this to-device kind is valid only when ServiceDescribe exposes a concrete recipient_device_id / queue target for the service DID; otherwise the service MUST expose a dedicated operation.

target_principal_id.description: Principal that owns target_source_ref (the to-device queue is addressed by (principal, device_id)). Carried so the relay routes directly without scanning Realm members to reverse-lookup the device's principal.

effective_scope.description: Tagged scope of the requested key material. Realm-default history uses {kind:'realm', realm_id}; Circle history uses {kind:'circle', realm_id, circle_id}.

policy_digest.description: Optional requester-observed policy digest hint. The key source MUST recompute the effective policy from accepted history before sharing.

membership_frontier_digest.description: Optional requester-observed membership frontier hint. The key source MUST recompute recipient eligibility from accepted history before sharing.

member_repair_request_content.description: ak.member.repair.request to-device content (contact-and-direct-conversation.md 8.2.1). A participant that has rejoined membership asks the current peer participant to author the MLS Remove/re-add Commit and Welcome that a replacement generation needs, because no actor may sign for another. Same non-authorizing trigger shape as ak.realm_key.request: it carries no Event bytes, no MLS material and no authority, and the peer MUST re-verify every gate from the signed event log before authoring anything.

realm_id.description: The pair's immutable Direct Conversation Realm. Repair never creates a successor Realm, Strand or binding.

requester_principal_id.description: MUST equal the principal bound by the selected device or Native-Agent authorization/evidence branch: no actor may ask for repair on another participant's behalf.

requester_device_id.description: Human-device branch only. MUST equal the detached repair authorization and portable device evidence device_id, and the exact KeyPackage selected by requester_keypackage_ref MUST belong to this current authorized device.

requester_agent_id.description: Native-Agent branch only. MUST equal requester_principal_id and the actor/subject of the accepted rejoin Event.

requester_agent_verification_method.description: Native-Agent runtime verification method that signed the repair authorization and the exact KeyPackage. It MUST match current AgentSignerEvidence byte for byte.

agent_key_authorize_event_id.description: Native-Agent branch current accepted ak.agent.key.authorize Event. It MUST match the current AgentSignerEvidence and the exact KeyPackage claim record.

requester_keypackage_ref.description: The single KeyPackage the peer claims for the re-add, so exactly one KeyPackage is consumed and the peer never has to guess which of the requester's packages to use.

observed_active_generation_value_digest.description: SHA-256 of RFC 8785 JCS for the complete accepted ak.component.direct_conversation.active_mls_generation.v1 cell value the requester observed, copied byte for byte from active_mls_generation_value_digest returned by the resolver. It is never derived from or replaced by active_mls_generation_ref. A peer that sees a different current whole-value digest MUST drop the request instead of authoring a second replacement.

rejoin_event_id.description: The requester's accepted ak.member.rejoin.own Event. The peer MUST verify it is accepted and subject-matched; an unaccepted or absent rejoin means there is nothing to repair yet.

purpose.description: Optional verification purpose. Omitted means generic device key verification. same_principal_device_authorization is used when a fresh device asks already authorized devices of the same principal to approve device authorization.

pairing_code.description: Eight-character human-readable Crockford-style device-pairing code bound into a same-principal authorization transcript. It is short-lived, one-time, and locked after ten failed submissions.

new_device_pubkey.description: Canonical PublicKey for the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization. kid MUST be the requesting ak:device:<uuidv7> id and the key material MUST be carried in key. The legacy {kid, alg, public_key} spelling is not canonical wire and MUST be rejected. The object is later consumed verbatim by ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

challenge_proof.description: Fresh requesting-device proof of possession over the ak.device-pairing.challenge.to_device.v1 transcript, which commits to {expires_at, gate_audience, new_device_pubkey_digest, pairing_code, request_canonical_digest, transaction_id}. The receiving authorized device MUST recompute the transcript from the values it displays to the user and verify the signature before treating the requesting device as pairable; it is later submitted verbatim to ak.gate.account.command.pair_device.

target_attestation.description: Closed accepted_device possession attestation of the requesting device when purpose=same_principal_device_authorization, and the only authority for its hpke_key and algorithms. It is the same schema and same domain the short-link path uses, because it binds only pairing_challenge_transcript_digest and each path already closes its own challenge transcript. The receiving authorized device MUST rebuild and verify it after the challenge proof, requiring device_id to equal new_device_pubkey.kid, device_public_key to decode to the same key as new_device_pubkey.key, and pairing_challenge_transcript_digest to equal the transcript digest it just recomputed; only then may it read hpke_key and algorithms from it and copy device_signature verbatim into the ak.device.authorize payload. It travels only on this out-of-band message and MUST NOT be posted back through the unauthenticated stage or resolve surface.

gate_audience.description: Auth Server audience/origin expected to consume the paired proof.

request_canonical_digest.description: Digest of the canonical request material bound into the pairing proof.

device_metadata.description: User-facing requesting-device hints. Receivers MUST treat this as display metadata and bind the parts shown to the user into the verification transcript.
